b2-04-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Bánk Asks of Tiborc
b2-04-01.scenario: In the palace corridor at midnight, Tiborc asks you, as a guard Bánk bán trusts, what Bánk told you to do. Bánk told you to let nobody enter the room.
b2-04-01.prompt: Tell Tiborc what Bánk bán asked you to do.
cues: Say what he asked: that nobody enter (use hogy + subjunctive)
b2-04-01.target: Bánk bán arra kért, hogy senki ne lépjen be a terembe.
b2-04-01.english: Bánk bán asked me that nobody enter the room.
b2-04-01.canDo: I can report what someone asks, demands or forbids, using hogy + the subjunctive.

b2-04-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Lest They Hear
b2-04-02.scenario: Tiborc asks you, one of Bánk bán's guards, why Bánk speaks to him alone in the room by the fireplace. You explain that he is careful so that others do not hear it.
b2-04-02.prompt: Tell Tiborc why Bánk bán talks to him alone.
cues: Say that others must not hear (use nehogy)
b2-04-02.target: Bánk bán óvatos, nehogy mások hallják.
b2-04-02.english: Bánk bán is careful lest others hear.
b2-04-02.canDo: I can construct negative purpose clauses using nehogy + subjunctive ('lest / so that ... not')

b2-04-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Are We to Do?
b2-04-03.scenario: Tiborc tells Bánk bán that the village has no bread left. You are Bánk bán and ask aloud what you should do for the people.
b2-04-03.prompt: Ask what you should do to help the people.
cues: Say the purpose: to help the people
b2-04-03.target: Mit tegyünk, hogy segítsünk az embereknek?
b2-04-03.english: What should we do to help the people?
b2-04-03.canDo: I can ask deliberative questions in the 1st person singular and plural subjunctive (Mit tegyek? Kihez forduljunk?)

b2-04-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Come What May
b2-04-04.scenario: A courtier warns Bánk bán that he will lose everything if he speaks against the queen. You are Bánk bán and answer him.
b2-04-04.prompt: Tell the courtier that whatever happens, you will follow your conscience.
b2-04-04.target: Történjék bármi, mindig a lelkiismeretemet követem!
b2-04-04.english: Come what may, I will always follow my conscience!
b2-04-04.canDo: I can form universal concessive clauses using verb-initial subjunctive inversion (Legyen bármilyen nehéz is...)

b2-04-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Bánk Promises Tiborc
b2-04-05.scenario: Tiborc has left the room in tears. A young servant asks you, Bánk bán, what you promised the old man.
b2-04-05.prompt: Tell the servant what you promised Tiborc, and why you will not stay silent.
cues: Say that you will go to the queen tonight
Say that you will not be silent any longer, lest the trouble grow
b2-04-05.target: Még ma éjjel a királyné elé állok. Nem hallgatok tovább, nehogy nagyobb baj legyen.
b2-04-05.english: Tonight I will go before the queen. I will not stay silent any longer, lest there be greater trouble.
b2-04-05.canDo: I can weave indirect commands, nehogy warnings, and concessive jussives into a cohesive persuasive speech

b2-04-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Rehearsal
b2-04-consolidation.scenario: A theatre director asks you, a young actor, what you were told about the rehearsal. The director told you to be on time and to speak carefully.
b2-04-consolidation.prompt: Tell the director what you were asked and why you are careful.
cues: Say what you were asked: not to be late
Say you are careful, lest you get into trouble
b2-04-consolidation.target: Arra kértek, hogy ne késsek el. Óvatosan beszélek, nehogy bajba kerüljek.
b2-04-consolidation.english: They asked me not to be late. I speak carefully lest I get into trouble.
b2-04-consolidation.canDo: I can accurately use indirect jussive clauses (arra kér / azt követeli, hogy + subjunctive) and negative purpose clauses with nehogy
